prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Heeeey reddit wtf is that and why isn't alcohol working?

This was my very first syngonium. I absolutely will. Not. Lose. It. It started my love for syngoniums and i just cannot lose it. I have sprayed this thing down so many times in the last few weeks. I've used peroxide, alcohol, insecticide, neem, I tried fungicide as a last ditch! What is is and how to I make them disappear!?

I've had a nasty mealy problem for the last year ish but haven't lost a plant yet. These didn't look like mealies to I wasn't too sure what to do and everything either reeks and isn't working or smells slightly better and still isn't working.

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely: young mealybugs (crawlers).** The tiny fuzzy white flecks on the leaf undersides look like juveniles, which fits the year-long mealybug problem in your collection. Sprays keep failing for two reasons. They miss the bugs and egg clusters hiding in the papery sheaths at the base of the stems. And no single spray kills the eggs, so new crawlers keep hatching.

Stop the peroxide, the fungicide and the rotation of different sprays. Fungicide does nothing to insects, and layering chemicals can burn the leaves. Some of the dull, browning foliage may be spray damage.

1. **Rinse today (10 min).** In the shower, tilt the pot and spray lukewarm water hard over the leaf undersides and down into the stem sheaths at soil level.
2. **Swab (10 min, every 5 days for 4 weeks).** Dip cotton swabs in 70% rubbing alcohol. Wipe every white speck, pushing into the sheaths and leaf joints.
3. **Insecticidal soap (5 min, every 7 days for 4 weeks).** Use a ready-to-use spray such as Safer Brand (~$10). Soak the undersides, stems and base until they drip. Do this on a different day from the swabbing.
4. **Isolate (5 min, once).** Move the plant at least a room away from your other plants until you've seen no specks for 3 weeks.
